requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than that of the existing command and control channel. The data may also be sent to an alternate network location from the main command and control server.

requirements.name: System Network Connections Discovery
requirements.reason: EC2 DescribeNetworkInterfaces and DescribeSecurityGroups are cloud configuration inventory calls, not evidence that a host queried live network connections; inspect host process and network telemetry.

requirements.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries. These interfaces and languages provide ways of interacting with computer systems and are a common feature across many different platforms. Most systems come with some built-in command-line interface and scripting capabilities, for example, macOS and Linux distributions include some flavor of Unix Shell while Windows installations include the Windows Command Shell and PowerShell.

requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion. Compromised credentials may be used to bypass access controls placed on various resources on systems within the network and may even be used for persistent access to remote systems and externally available services, such as VPNs, Outlook Web Access, network devices, and remote desktop.[1] Compromised credentials may also grant an adversary increased privilege to specific systems or access to restricted areas of the network. Adversaries may choose not to use malware or tools in conjunction with the legitimate access those credentials provide to make it harder to detect their presence. requirements.name: Account Discovery
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of valid accounts, usernames, or email addresses on a system or within a compromised environment. This information can help adversaries determine which accounts exist, which can aid in follow-on behavior such as brute-forcing, spear-phishing attacks, or account takeovers (e.g., Valid Accounts).

requirements.name: Account Manipulation
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain access to victim systems. Account manipulation may consist of any action that preserves adversary access to a compromised account, such as modifying credentials or permission groups. These actions could also include account activity designed to subvert security policies, such as performing iterative password updates to bypass password duration policies and preserve the life of compromised credentials.

requirements.name: Brute Force
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to gain access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained. Without knowledge of the password for an account or set of accounts, an adversary may systematically guess the password using a repetitive or iterative mechanism. Brute forcing passwords can take place via interaction with a service that will check the validity of those credentials or offline against previously acquired credential data, such as password hashes.

requirements.name: Automated Collection
requirements.reason: Native checks test only the listed AWS configuration or activity signals. Uncovered remainder: Once established within a system or network, an adversary may use automated techniques for collecting internal data. Methods for performing this technique could include use of a Command and Scripting Interpreter to search for and copy information fitting set criteria such as file type, location, or name at specific time intervals. In cloud-based environments, adversaries may also use cloud APIs, command line interfaces, or extract, transform, and load (ETL) services to automatically collect data. This functionality could also be built into remote access tools.

Unlike Upload Malware, this technique focuses on adversaries implanting an image in a registry within a victim’s environment. frameworks.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-171 Revision 2

requirements.name: 3.11.2 Scan for vulnerabilities in organizational systems and applications periodically and when new vulnerabilities affecting those systems and applications are identified
requirements.reason: No indexed native evaluator verifies this control: Organizations determine the required vulnerability scanning for all system components, ensuring that potential sources of vulnerabilities such as networked printers, scanners, and copiers are not overlooked. The vulnerabilities to be scanned are readily updated as new vulnerabilities are discovered, announced, and scanning methods developed. This process ensures that potential vulnerabilities in the system are identified and addressed as quickly as possible. Vulnerability analyses for custom software applications may require additional approaches such as static analysis, dynamic analysis, binary analysis, or a hybrid of the three approaches. Organizations can employ these analysis approaches in source code reviews and in a variety of tools (e.g., static analysis tools, web-based application scanners, binary analyzers) and in source code reviews. Vulnerability scanning includes: scanning for patch levels; scanning for functions, ports, protocols, and services that should not be accessible to users or devices; and scanning for improperly configured or incorrectly operating information flow control mechanisms. To facilitate interoperability, organizations consider using products that are Security Content Automated Protocol (SCAP)-validated, scanning tools that express vulnerabilities in the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) naming convention, and that employ the Open Vulnerability Assessment Language (OVAL) to determine the presence of system vulnerabilities. Sources for vulnerability information include the Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) listing and the National Vulnerability Database (NVD). Security assessments, such as red team exercises, provide additional sources of potential vulnerabilities for which to scan. Organizations also consider using scanning tools that express vulnerability impact by the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). In certain situations, the nature of the vulnerability scanning may be more intrusive or the system component that is the subject of the scanning may contain highly sensitive information. Privileged access authorization to selected system components facilitates thorough vulnerability scanning and protects the sensitive nature of such scanning. Examine scan results, risk decisions and remediation tickets to establish the stated requirement.

Enforcement occurs in boundary protection devices (e.g., gateways, routers, guards, encrypted tunnels, firewalls) that employ rule sets or establish configuration settings that restrict system services, provide a packetfiltering capability based on header information, or message-filtering capability based on message content (e.g., implementing key word searches or using document characteristics). Organizations also consider the trustworthiness of filtering and inspection mechanisms (i.e., hardware, firmware, and software components) that are critical to information flow enforcement. In such situations, information owners or stewards provide guidance at designated policy enforcement points between interconnected systems. Organizations consider mandating specific architectural solutions when required to enforce specific security policies. Enforcement includes: prohibiting information transfers between interconnected systems (i.e., allowing access only); employing hardware mechanisms to enforce one-way information flows; and implementing trustworthy regrading mechanisms to reassign security attributes and security labels. Monitoring and auditing requirements can be balanced with other system needs. Organizations consider limiting the additional audit log information to only that information explicitly needed for specific audit requirements. This facilitates the use of audit trails and audit logs by not including information that could potentially be misleading or could make it more difficult to locate information of interest. frameworks.name: Prowler ThreatScore Compliance Framework for Azure

requirements.reason: The evaluator checks MFA method registration capability for active privileged users; it explicitly does not test Conditional Access enforcement or per-sign-in MFA.
The evaluator checks MFA method registration capability for enabled non-privileged users; registration alone does not enforce MFA at sign-in.
The Conditional Access evaluator finds a declared MFA policy for Azure management API but does not inspect exclusions or effective authentication strength.
The Conditional Access evaluator finds a declared MFA policy for admin portals but does not inspect exclusions or effective authentication strength.
The evaluator checks MFA registration capability for users with VM RBAC roles, not effective MFA enforcement on VM access.

The requirement asks for Ensure that 'Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants' is set to 'Yes'. The mapped evaluator tests bad=(True,), good=(False,); the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The evaluator counts distinct principal IDs in active Global Administrator directory-role assignments. It does not expand group assignments into effective users or include PIM eligible assignments, so it cannot prove that fewer than five users hold the role.

The requirement asks for Ensure That 'Guest users access restrictions' is set to 'Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory obj. The mapped evaluator tests Entra ID guest access is restricted to their own directory objects; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

Native semantic scope: azure.claude.entra_user_consent_disabled: Default role self-consent policy assignment only. Existing grants and all effective consent capabilities remain unverified. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.

The evaluator only rejects the unrestricted legacy consent policy. A policy permitting broad unverified publishers would still pass, so verified-publisher-only consent is not established. Corrected native semantic scope: azure.claude.entra_user_consent_not_legacy: Default role legacy self-consent assignment only. Custom grant definitions and existing application consents remain unverified. Manual or separate-check evidence is required for the stated remainder.
The requirement asks for Ensure Trusted Locations Are Defined. The mapped evaluator tests Entra ID defines a trusted IP named location; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that 'Users can create security groups in Azure portals, API or PowerShell' is set to 'No'. The mapped evaluator tests bad=(True,), good=(False,); the listed checks directly cover this setting.
The requirement asks for Ensure That ‘Users Can Register Applications’ Is Set to ‘No’. The mapped evaluator tests bad=(True,), good=(False,); the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The evaluator accepts both adminsAndGuestInviters and none. The named setting requires the specific admin-role option; a tenant configured to allow no guest invitations would pass this check without having that setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that 'Users can create Microsoft 365 groups in Azure portals, API or PowerShell' is set to 'No'. The mapped evaluator tests Entra ID restricts Microsoft 365 group creation; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The NSG evaluator detects declared Internet-source inbound Allow rules for TCP 3389. It does not resolve effective routes, other network controls, or evidence that Internet RDP access was evaluated and approved.

The NSG evaluator detects declared Internet-source inbound Allow rules for TCP 22. It does not resolve effective routes, other network controls, or evidence that Internet SSH access was evaluated and approved.

The NSG evaluator detects declared Internet-source inbound UDP Allow rules. It does not resolve effective routes, other network controls, or evidence that Internet UDP access was evaluated and approved.
The NSG evaluator reads internet inbound Allow rules for TCP 80 only; the requirement explicitly includes HTTPS. A second read-only rule check is needed for TCP 443.
The requirement asks for Ensure an Azure Bastion Host Exists. The mapped evaluator tests Subscription has at least one Azure Bastion host; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that Microsoft Entra authentication is Configured for SQL Servers. The mapped evaluator tests SQL server has a Microsoft Entra administrator; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure no Azure SQL Databases allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0. The mapped evaluator tests SQL firewall rule does not span 0.0.0.0-255.255.255.255; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure 'Allow public access from any Azure service within Azure to this server' for PostgreSQL flexible server is disabled. The mapped evaluator tests PostgreSQL flexible server does not allow access from all Azure services; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The evaluator checks only Cosmos DB isVirtualNetworkFilterEnabled. It does not inspect the allowed virtual-network or IP rules; an enabled filter can still admit broad networks, so selected-network restriction is not established.
The evaluator tests a private endpoint only on Cosmos DB accounts. The generic control covers other eligible Azure services.

The evaluator checks only Cosmos DB disableLocalAuth. It does not verify Entra ID client authentication, effective Cosmos DB data-plane RBAC grants, or whether key authentication remains necessary under the stated exception.
The requirement asks for Ensure that 'Public Network Access' is 'Disabled' for storage accounts. The mapped evaluator tests bad=Enabled, good=Disabled; the listed checks directly cover this setting.
The requirement asks for Ensure Default Network Access Rule for Storage Accounts is Set to Deny. The mapped evaluator tests bad=Allow, good=Deny; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure 'Allow Azure services on the trusted services list to access this storage account' is Enabled for Storage Account Access. The mapped evaluator tests Storage network rules let trusted Azure services bypass; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The evaluator finds at least one private endpoint connection on a storage account. It does not require an approved connection for every used storage subresource or establish that clients actually use private endpoints.
The evaluator tests the App Service Easy Auth platform.enabled switch for kind app*. It does not verify a configured identity provider or effective authentication requirements for application routes.
The requirement asks for Ensure 'FTP State' is set to 'FTPS Only' or 'Disabled'. The mapped evaluator tests App Service forbids plain FTP; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure server parameter 'log_checkpoints' is set to 'ON' for PostgreSQL flexible server. The mapped evaluator tests bad=('off',), good=('on',); the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure server parameter 'connection_throttle.enable' is set to 'ON' for PostgreSQL flexible server. The mapped evaluator tests bad=('off',), good=('on',); the listed checks directly cover this setting.

Ensure server parameter 'log_connections' is set to 'ON' for PostgreSQL single server Inspect new read-only Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/servers/configurations GET: name, properties.value for log_connections; FAIL if log_connections is not ON on a still-existing PostgreSQL single server.

Ensure server parameter 'log_disconnections' is set to 'ON' for PostgreSQL single server Inspect new read-only Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/servers/configurations GET: name, properties.value for log_disconnections; FAIL if log_disconnections is not ON on a still-existing PostgreSQL single server.

The requirement asks for Ensure server parameter 'audit_log_enabled' is set to 'ON' for MySQL flexible server. The mapped evaluator tests bad=('off',), good=('on',); the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure server parameter 'audit_log_events' has 'CONNECTION' set for MySQL flexible server. The mapped evaluator tests MySQL flexible server audit log records CONNECTION events; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The evaluator recognizes an enabled AuditEvent category, but its category-group branch requires both audit and allLogs in one setting. A vault using either documented group alone is not accepted; logging enabled through that configuration is not fully evaluated.
The evaluator checks enabled flow logs and Traffic Analytics, but does not verify the stated Log Analytics destination.

The requirement asks for Ensure that logging for Azure AppService 'HTTP logs' is enabled. The mapped evaluator tests App Service app (kind app*) sends HTTP logs (or allLogs) through a diagnostic setting; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure server parameter 'logfiles.retention_days' is greater than 3 days for PostgreSQL flexible server. The mapped evaluator tests PostgreSQL flexible server retains server logs for more than 3 days; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that a 'Diagnostic Setting' exists for Subscription Activity Logs. The mapped evaluator tests Subscription exports the activity log through a diagnostic setting; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that 'Auditing' Retention is 'greater than 90 days'. The mapped evaluator tests SQL auditing is enabled with retention above 90 days or unlimited; the listed checks directly cover this setting.
The requirement asks for Ensure that 'Auditing' is set to 'On'. The mapped evaluator tests bad=Disabled, good=Enabled; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that Activity Log Alert exists for Delete SQL Server Firewall Rule. The mapped evaluator tests Enabled activity log alert exists for Delete SQL Server Firewall Rule; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that Activity Log Alert exists for Create or Update Public IP Address rule. The mapped evaluator tests Enabled activity log alert exists for Create or Update Public IP Address; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that Activity Log Alert exists for Delete Public IP Address rule. The mapped evaluator tests Enabled activity log alert exists for Delete Public IP Address; the listed checks directly cover this setting.
The evaluator only requires at least one Application Insights component in the subscription, not instrumentation of every App Service.
The evaluator compares Network Watcher with VNet regions; it does not establish every Azure region in use by non-VNet resources.
The Defender assessment evaluator checks named reported assessment states and returns not applicable if absent; it does not enumerate all VMs or prove endpoint agents installed on each.

The evaluator checks reported Healthy or Unhealthy states for three named Defender assessments, including system updates. It returns not applicable when a named assessment is absent and does not enumerate every machine or prove that the Apply system updates recommendation is Completed for each applicable resource.

The evaluator checks enforcementMode only for the SecurityCenterBuiltIn policy assignment. It does not inspect whether individual Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark policy definitions or overrides are Disabled.

The requirement asks for Ensure That 'All users with the following roles' is set to 'Owner'. The mapped evaluator tests Defender contact role notifications are On and include Owner; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure 'Additional email addresses' is Configured with a Security Contact Email. The mapped evaluator tests Defender security contact lists at least one email address; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure Diagnostic Setting captures appropriate categories. The mapped evaluator tests A subscription diagnostic setting captures Administrative, Security, Alert and Policy; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The evaluator accepts Low, Medium, or High as the minimum alert severity and reads the last non-null Alert notification source. The requirement specifies High; it does not verify that exact configured value across every source.

The requirement asks for Ensure That Microsoft Defender for DNS Is Set To 'On'. The mapped evaluator tests Defender Dns plan is Standard where the plan is still offered; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that Activity Log Alert exists for Create Policy Assignment. The mapped evaluator tests Enabled activity log alert exists for Create Policy Assignment; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

The requirement asks for Ensure that Activity Log Alert exists for Delete Network Security Group. The mapped evaluator tests Enabled activity log alert exists for Delete Network Security Group; the listed checks directly cover this setting.

requirements.reason: The requirement calls for Ensure User-Managed/External Keys for Service Accounts Are Rotated Every 90 Days or Fewer. The selected evaluator tests keyType, which covers that GCP setting.

The requirement calls for Ensure API Keys Only Exist for Active Services. The proposed read-only predicate detects an active key without declared API target restrictions; a PASS proves only named target presence, while a broad cloudapis.googleapis.com target remains UNKNOWN. It does not prove that target services are active or owner-approved, that only required services are allowed, or that client restrictions exist. These remaining criteria require authoritative service-activation and owner-policy evidence plus separate client-restriction review. The removed Project has no API keys mapping tests a different predicate.
The requirement calls for Ensure API Keys Are Rotated Every 90 Days. The selected evaluator tests createTime, deleteTime, which covers that GCP setting.
The requirement calls for Ensure That There Are Only GCP-Managed Service Account Keys for Each Service Account. The selected evaluator tests keyType, which covers that GCP setting.

proposed_checks.description: Detects Pods without an imagePullSecrets reference; private registry pulls may fail or use unintended credentials.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Create a docker-registry Secret in the Pod namespace and add its name under spec.imagePullSecrets in the Pod template.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected pod.metadata.namespace/spec.serviceAccountName, rolebinding/clusterrolebinding.metadata.namespace and subjects[].kind/name/namespace.
proposed_checks.predicate: For every pod, a rolebinding in pod.metadata.namespace or a clusterrolebinding has a ServiceAccount subject with namespace=pod.metadata.namespace and name=(pod.spec.serviceAccountName or "default"); UNKNOWN on incomplete inventory.
proposed_checks.title: Pod ServiceAccount has RBAC binding
proposed_checks.description: Detects Pod ServiceAccounts that do not appear in a RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding; expected workload permissions may be missing.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Create a namespace scoped RoleBinding for the Pod’s effective spec.serviceAccountName and the minimum required Role.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected role/clusterrole.rules[].resources/verbs, rolebinding/clusterrolebinding.subjects/roleRef, pod.metadata.namespace and spec.containers[].securityContext.privileged; mandatory authorization lists.
proposed_checks.predicate: For each effective RBAC binding, grants on pods/exec:create and pods/ephemeralcontainers:update belong to authorized_subjects; each privileged utility pod namespace belongs to authorized_utility_namespaces; UNKNOWN without mandatory lists or resolved RBAC rules.
proposed_checks.title: Restrict Kubernetes privileged utilities
proposed_checks.description: Detects subjects with unapproved pods/exec or pods/ephemeralcontainers grants, or privileged utility Pods outside authorized namespaces; debugging access can expose workloads.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Remove unapproved RBAC grants for pods/exec create and pods/ephemeralcontainers update, and restrict privileged utility Pods to authorized namespaces.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected rolebinding/clusterrolebinding.metadata.namespace, subjects[].kind/name/namespace, roleRef.kind/name; mandatory required subject, role and allowed namespace inputs.
proposed_checks.predicate: At least one rolebinding or clusterrolebinding in allowed_namespaces has subjects[].kind/name equal to required_subject_kind/name and roleRef.kind/name equal to required_role_kind/name; UNKNOWN without policy inputs or complete inventory.
proposed_checks.title: Response team has required RBAC binding
proposed_checks.description: Detects absence of the specified response team RBAC binding; responders may lack the permissions needed for incident action.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Create a RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding for the required response team subject and required Role or ClusterRole within an allowed namespace.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected secret_metadata.metadata.deletionTimestamp/name/namespace from metadata-only LIST /api/v1/secrets.
proposed_checks.predicate: For each secret_metadata, metadata.deletionTimestamp is null or absent; UNKNOWN if metadata-only Secret inventory is incomplete.
proposed_checks.title: Checks if Kubernetes Secrets are not marked for deletion. The rule is NON_COMPLIANT if Secrets are scheduled for deletio
proposed_checks.description: Detects Secrets with a non-null deletionTimestamp; pending deletion can break workloads that depend on them.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Remove stale workload references and recreate the Secret with the required data if it is still needed; update the controller to preserve it.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected service.metadata.name/namespace, spec.type, spec.externalTrafficPolicy; mandatory in_scope_service_names and required_external_traffic_policy.
proposed_checks.predicate: For each service whose metadata.name belongs to in_scope_service_names and spec.type="LoadBalancer", spec.externalTrafficPolicy=required_external_traffic_policy; UNKNOWN without policy inputs or complete inventory.
proposed_checks.title: LoadBalancer external traffic policy matches required value
proposed_checks.description: Detects selected LoadBalancer Services whose externalTrafficPolicy differs from the required value; traffic routing may bypass the expected source IP or node behavior.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Set spec.externalTrafficPolicy to required_external_traffic_policy (Local or Cluster) on each selected LoadBalancer Service manifest.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected service.spec.type and metadata.namespace; mandatory authorized_namespaces.
proposed_checks.predicate: For each service with spec.type="LoadBalancer", metadata.namespace belongs to authorized_namespaces; UNKNOWN without the mandatory set.
proposed_checks.title: Checks if LoadBalancers are associated with an authorized Kubernetes Namespace
proposed_checks.description: Detects LoadBalancer Services outside authorized namespaces; public endpoints can appear in unapproved workloads.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Move the Service to an authorized namespace or change spec.type to ClusterIP if external exposure is unnecessary.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected service.spec.type and spec.ports[].protocol/port.
proposed_checks.predicate: For each service with spec.type="ClusterIP", no spec.ports[] entry has protocol TCP (or omitted TCP default) and port=21; UNKNOWN on incomplete inventory.

proposed_checks.description: Detects ClusterIP Services declaring TCP port 21; the conventional FTP port can carry credentials without encryption.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Remove port 21 from spec.ports or migrate the application to an encrypted protocol and update the Service port.

proposed_checks.data_source: Collected service.spec.type; mandatory serviceType policy input.
proposed_checks.predicate: For each service, spec.type equals required serviceType; UNKNOWN when the mandatory parameter or inventory is unavailable.

proposed_checks.description: Detects Services whose type differs from the required serviceType parameter; the endpoint may have unintended exposure or availability.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: Set spec.type in the Service manifest to the approved serviceType value and apply the manifest.

proposed_checks.data_source: Complete Service spec.type and an explicit owner-approved set of Services that require external load balancers.
proposed_checks.predicate: For a Service explicitly selected by owner policy, PASS when spec.type is LoadBalancer and FAIL when a complete observed type differs; UNKNOWN when approved selection, type, or inventory completeness is missing; Services outside the selected set are NOT_APPLICABLE.

proposed_checks.description: Checks LoadBalancer type only for Services explicitly selected by owner policy; no universal external-exposure requirement is inferred.
proposed_checks.remediation_hint: For an owner-approved external Service, review exposure and provider annotations before changing spec.type to LoadBalancer.
